questions.question: In which Indian state the archaeological site of the Paleolithic period, the "Bhimbetka Rock Shelters" is situated?
questions.solution:
• The **Bhimbetka Rock Shelters** are situated in the **Raisen District of Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• The site is the earliest evidence of human evidence on the Indian Subcontinent.
 
• The name of the archaeological site is related to the Hindu deity ‘Bheem’ and roughly translates to the sitting place of Bheem.

questions.question: Who among the following drafted the 'Pakistan Resolution'?
questions.solution:
• **Maulvi A.K. Fazlul Huq** drafted the Pakistan Resoution.
 
• The early idea was to have greater Muslim autonomy in British India, but after discussion a new separate Muslim state was called upon for.
 
• This resolution was first presented in Minto Park situated in Lahore.

questions.question: How has India been described in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
• India is described as a **Union of several States** in **Article 1** of the Constitution Of India.
 
• The Article states ‘The territory of India shall consist of: The territories of the states, The Union territories and Any territory that may be acquired’.
 
• As of present India consists of **28** such **States** and **8 Union Territories**.

questions.question: How many types of writs have been mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
There are **5 types** **of writs** mentioned in the Indian Constitution.

A writ is a written document issuing a legal order, it is a type of order that is usually issued by a court of law.

The writs mentioned are as follows:

 
• Habeas Corpus
 
• Mandamus
 
• Certiorari
 
• Prohibition
 
• Quo Warranto

questions.question: What is NABARD?
questions.solution:
• **NABARD** is a **specialised government bank to help agricultural sector**.
 
• It stands for **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development** and is **headquartered** in **Mumbai** with several regional offices throughout the country.
 
• Its duties are of providing and regulating credit and other facilities for the promotion and development of agriculture, small-scale industries, cottage and village industries, handicrafts and other rural crafts.

questions.question: What is the full form of CSO?
questions.solution:
• **CSO** stands for **Central Statistical Organisation**, it is a government agency under the **Ministry** **of Statistics and Programme Implementation**.
 
• The main aim of this agency is to provide advisory services to other statistical agencies, keeping public relations with international statistical bodies, preparing and publishing national accounts statistics, industrial statistics, conducting economic census and training statistical personnel.

questions.question: What is the rank of India in terms of ‘area’, among the countries of the world?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **India** is the **seventh largest country__** in the world in terms of land area.
 
• It has a **total area** of about **3.287 million kilometre squares.**
 
• It falls behind Australia with an area of 7.617 million kilometre squares.

questions.question: What is Kuiper belt?

options.text: Planetary bodies that orbit around Jupiter
Icy planetary bodies near Neptune that orbit the sun

questions.solution:
• **Kuiper belt** is the collection of icy planetary bodies that orbit around Neptune.
 
• It is also known as the **Edgeworth–Kuiper belt**.
 
• The region of the Solar system that exists beyond the planets, extending from the orbit of Neptune (at 30 AU) to approximately 50 AU from the Sun, is given the name ‘Kuiper Belt’.

questions.question: Which among the following is NOT a micronutrient for plants?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The essential elements required for plant growth and metabolism are divided into two main categories:

 
• Macronutrients/Macroelements: Macronutrients are generally present in plant tissues in large amounts (in excess of 10 mmole/kg of dry matter)

__
 
• The macronutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorous, sulphur, potassium, calcium, and magnesium.

 2.Micronutrients/Microelements: Also called trace elements. These are needed in very small amounts (less than 10 mmole/kg of dry matter)

 
• These include iron, manganese, copper, molybdenum, zinc, boron, chlorine, and nickel

Explanation:__

 
• **Nitrogen** is **not a micronutrient for plants** from the options listed above.
 
• Micronutrients are those elements that are required by the plants in small quantities for their proper functioning.
 
• **Nitrogen** is a **macronutrient**, which means it is required in much larger quantities.
 
• It is a **major component of chlorophyll**, which is the pigment responsible for photosynthesis. It is also a **part of amino acids** which are sub-blocks of proteins in plants.

questions.question: What is the main function of ribosomes in the cell?

options.text: None of the option is correct

questions.solution:
• The main function of **ribosomes** is the **synthesis of vital proteins** inside the cell.
 
• The ribosome molecules link amino acids, which are the building blocks of protein structures, in different combinations to form different proteins.
 
• The linking process is governed by messenger RNA molecules.
 
•

questions.question: The edible part of an onion is __________.
questions.solution:
• The **fleshy leaves** of an onion are its consumable part.
 
• As a whole the **onion is a bulb**, which is a short modified form of a stem which is surrounded by these fleshy leaves that store food for the onion shoots.

questions.question: Not servicing the vehicles results in incomplete combustion of carbonaceous matter in automobile engine which generates: _________.
questions.solution:
• The incomplete combustion of the carbon content in the fuel leads to the generation of **Carbon monoxide (CO)**.
 
• This is called incomplete oxidation of the fuel because of lack of oxygen and servicing of vehicle.
 
• Carbon monoxide is very harmful to the human body as it can cause ‘Carbon monoxide poisoning’ which prevents ‘haemoglobin’ to carry oxygen in the human body.

questions.question: The fibre least prone to catch fire is ____________.
questions.solution:
• The fibre least prone to catch fire among the given option is **Cotton**.
 
• **Pyrolysis** is the term given to the phenomenon of decomposition of material due to fire.
 
• Fibres catch fire when the surrounding temperature reaches above their respective **flash** **point** temperature.
 
• **Cotton** is a **natural fibre** consisting of ‘Cellulose’ while the **others** are **man-made fibres**.

questions.question: What is used to check the development of infant in the uterus?
questions.solution:
__**Ultrasound**__ is used to check the development of a fetus developing inside the womb.

 
• Ultrasound is preferred because it is not harmful to the human body and ultrasound is a non-invasive technique so there is a minimum risk during inspecting of the delicate infant.

questions.question: Which one of the following has the highest value of specific heat?
questions.solution:
• **Water** has the highest value of specific heat amongst the substances listed.
 
• The specific heat of an object is the amount of heat per unit mass required to raise the temperature by one degree Celsius.
 
• In other words it is a measure of a substance’s sensitivity to heat.
 
• The **specific heat of water** is about **4186 J/Kg K**.

questions.question: The key results of United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) meeting held recently is to restrict global warming by keeping temperature rise ________.
questions.solution:
• In the meeting, it was agreed upon to restrict temperature rise to **below 2°C**.
 
• It is also famously known as **The Paris Agreement** because the meeting took place in the city of Paris.
 
• The agreement is signed so that countries reduce their greenhouse emissions to prevent global warming and its catastrophic effects on the planet.

questions.question: Operating system is also called the ___________ between the user and computer.
questions.solution:
• The **Operating System** is the **Interface between the user and the computer**.
 
• It is called the Interface because it converts the commands given by the user to language that the computer can understand (machine language) and vice a versa.
 
• There are many operating systems available such as Windows, Mac OS and Linux.

questions.question: In which state of India is the Pushkar Mela held in?
questions.solution:
• The **Pushkar Mela** is a fair that is held in **Pushkar town of Rajasthan**.
 
• It is one of the country’s largest livestock fair and cultural gathering.

questions.question: Who among the following invented the jet engine?
questions.solution:
• **Frank Whittle** is the inventor of the **jet engine**.
 
• He was a British Royal Air Force Officer who put forward the idea of the turbojet engine in his senior thesis at the Royal Air Force College in the year of 1928.

questions.question: Which country recently launched Tiantong-1 satellites for mobile communication?
questions.solution:
• The **Tiantong-1** was developed by the **China Aerospace Science and Technology Corporation.**
 
• It is a **mobile communications satellite** meant for use in the China Mobile Multimedia Broadcasting project.
 
• It was launched on **August 5 2016**.

questions.question: Who has authored the book, titled** 'Wealth of Nations'?**
questions.solution:
• The ‘**Wealth of Nations**’ is authored by **Adam Smith**.
 
• He was a Scottish economist and a moral philosopher.
 
• The book was published in 1776 and is considered as a very important piece of economic literature as it was one of the first books which explained how a nation built its wealth back in that period.

questions.question: Which county will host the 2018 Asian Games?
questions.solution:
• The **2018 Asian Games** were held in **Indonesia** and were also known as the **Jakarta-Palembang 2018**.
 
• This year marked the 18th year for the Pan-Asia multisport event.

questions.question: How is January 9 celebrated every year by the Government of India?
questions.solution:
• **January 9** is annually celebrated as the **Pravasi Bharatiya Divas**.
 
• It is a day observed to celebrate the contribution of the overseas Indian community in development of the nation.
 
• It is also the day Mahatma Gandhi returned from South Africa to India in 1915.

questions.question: Who among the following was conferred with the 47th Dadasaheb Phalke Award at the 63rd National Awards?
questions.solution:
• **Manoj Kumar** was awarded with the **47th Dadasaheb Phalke Award.**
 
• It was awarded to him by the **President of India** for his outstanding contribution to the film industry on 22ⁿd December at the 63rd National Awards.

questions.question: Which of the following is world's first country to have cashless economy?
questions.solution:
• **Sweden** is the world’s first country to have completely eliminated paper currency.
 
• Only about 1% of all the payments made in the country were by using cash in 2016 and the number has reduced since then.
